entities.summary: Domingo Paes was a traveller from Portuguese India, who visited the Vijayanagara Empire, located on the southern portion of the Deccan Plateau in around 1520. He journeyed together with a group of traders from what was then Portuguese Goa, which was the capital of other territories such as Portuguese Bombay. His visit took place during the reign of the Emperor Krishnadevaraya, Paes recorded his impressions of Vijayanagara in his work Chronica dos reis de Bisnaga. His detailed account is one of the few known descriptions of that empire and of its capital, Vijayanagara (Hampi), by a chronicler from abroad.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Domingo Paes' account of Vijayanagara provides a rare external perspective on the empire's culture and politics during its reign under Krishnadevaraya. His work is significant for historians studying the exchange between Indian and European cultures during this period.
